key_insight: A transformer can infer reward preferences from a few demonstrations, but robust adaptation to unseen human preference domains requires an added signal such as response time.
engineering_relevance: This enables more flexible RLHF systems that can generalize across heterogeneous user values without retraining a separate reward model for every new domain.
method: Use in-context preference demonstrations to infer latent reward structure on the fly.
Augment the transformer input with human response time as an auxiliary signal.
Compare standard transformer behavior against the adapted model to assess unseen-domain generalization.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports characterizing an asymptotic bias in a standard transformer and showing that adding response time enables successful adaptation to previously unseen preference domains.
watch_item: Response time must be reliably measured and may introduce sensitivity to noisy or context-dependent human interaction signals.
paper_title: In-Context Reward Adaptation for Robust Preference Modeling
